saints.name: St. Casimir
saints.title: Prince of Poland
saints.shortBlurb: The chaste young prince of Poland who chose prayer and the poor over the ambitions of a crown…
biography: Born at Wawel Castle in Kraków on 3 October 1458, the second son of King Casimir IV of Poland and Elizabeth of Austria, Casimir was educated from the age of nine by the chronicler Jan Długosz in Latin, law, and history.

In 1471 his father sent him with an army of twelve thousand to take the crown of Hungary. Convinced the enterprise was unjust, he withdrew from the campaign and afterward refused to renew it; he likewise declined a marriage arranged with Kunigunde, daughter of the Emperor Frederick III, preferring celibacy.

Heir to the throne after his brother Vladislaus became king of Bohemia, he gave himself to prayer, fasting, and almsgiving, often found kneeling at locked church doors before dawn. A copy of the hymn "Omni die dic Mariae" was found in his coffin, and it is still called the Hymn of St. Casimir.

He died of tuberculosis at Grodno on 4 March 1484, aged twenty-five, and was buried in Vilnius Cathedral. Tradition holds that Pope Leo X canonized him in 1521 at the petition of his brother King Sigismund I. Prince of both nations and buried in the Lithuanian capital, he is venerated as patron of Poland and Lithuania.
saints.knownFor: His purity, devotion to Our Lady, and care for the poor.

canonization.canonized: Canonized 1521 (bull of Pope Leo X); confirmed 1602 by Pope Clement VIII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 March
